_: The film language of “The Power of the Incomprehensible” (docs/stories/sila-nepost.md): 1910s silent cinema — tripod, frontal staging, the iris, close-ups of faces, intertitles; autochrome colour — only while that music plays.

language.editing: Shots of 8–30 s, simple cuts; scenes open and close with an iris (in: iris), chapters and the epigraph are intertitles on black. No dissolves; the rhythm is like a silent-film pianist's: slow, with pauses.
language.camera: Tripod, no shake (hand 0). The camera frontal, at chest height, as in a theatre: a wide “stage” shot, then close-ups of faces (the iris may close in on a face). Camera movement is rare and short — a slight push-in (push 4–8) on a face at the climax.
language.people: The acting pantomime of silent film: clear, expressive poses, in profile or ¾, a gesture reads without words. Faces — make-up: pale, with dark eyes.
language.light_color: Reality — b/w toned per scene (grade: saturation 0 + tint): amber — interiors, blue — night, sepia — the street, green — the asylum. Light and shadows painted on the sets. When that music plays (a dream, hypnosis, flashes in the asylum), the image comes through in autochrome colour (grade_to: saturation 1, autochrome 1); the music is torn away — the colour fades.
language.elements: Projector flicker, film scratches and dust, a “hand-cranked” 18 fps — for the whole film (the style's stage). An open window, the light from it, a curtain.
language.time: Pauses after key phrases (holds) of 2–6 s; at the climax — silence and colour instead of sound.
language.sound: A silent-film pianist: a quiet piano or harmonium, the projector's rattle; that music itself is never played — a hum (drone) and silence; the lie about Schubert — a music-box phrase.
